sentences.text: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.K. GUPTA  ORDER (Delivered on this day of 5th May, 2016)

The applicants have preferred the present petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. against the order dated 03.11.2010 passed by 10th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior in Criminal Revision No. 509/2010, whereby the revision was dismissed and order dated 19.08.2010 passed by the JMFC, Gwalior in Criminal Case No. 6257/2006 was maintained in which charges of offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (in short "P.F. Act") were framed against each of the applicant.
The applicants have also challenged the order dated 19.08.2010 passed by the JMFC, Gwalior.

(2) Facts of the case, in short, are that the respondent- Food Inspector had lodged a criminal complaint against the applicants and other accused persons that on 27.02.1992 at 05:00 PM, he inspected the shop of applicant No. 3 Shankarlal and sons and inspected the sealed packets of Bhola Chhap Jafrani Patti Tobacco having 50 gm tobacco in each packet and thereafter the proceeding of seizure was started.
Sample was sent for analysis and thereafter getting the report from Public Analyst, the complaint was filed.
The trial Court has framed the aforesaid charges vide order dated 19.08.2010.
(3) I have heard the learned counsel for the parties.
(4) In the present case, due to subsequent event, it would not be appropriate to decide the matter on merits.
During the pendency of this petition, the applicant No. 1 Suresh Chand Chaurasiya has died and, hence, trial against his shall be abated.
The applicant No. 3 was a partnership firm and other partners of the firm namely Shankarlal and Ramesh Chand have already expired during the pendency of the trial.

It would be apparent from the documents annexed with the complaint that Smt. Geeta Chaurasiya was not present at the spot, when the sample was taken and, therefore,

sentences.text: the light of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in case of "Smt. Manibai and another Vs. State of Maharashtra" [AIR 1974 SC 434], the sleeping partner could not be prosecuted for offence of food adulteration done by the partnership firm.

entities.text: Smt. Manibai and another Vs. State of Maharashtra" [AIR 1974 SC 434]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the applicant No. 2 Smt. Geeta Chaurasiya cannot be prosecuted for aforesaid adulteration, hence, except Smt. Geeta Chaurasiya, when no partner remained alive of the applicant No. 3 then no such prosecution can take place against the applicant No. 3 because no one represents the applicant No. 3 at present and in case of conviction, no one can be sent to the jail to execute the sentence.
Hence, on death of the applicant No. 1, the trial against the applicant No. 3 also abates as the applicant No. 2 is absolved from her liability.
(5) On the basis of the aforesaid discussions, the present petition is hereby allowed.

Charges framed against Smt.
Geeta Chaurasiya are quashed.
She is discharged from charge of Section 7/16 of the P.F. Act.
The applicant No. 1 has expired and trial against him shall be abated and in absence of any partner representing the firm, the applicant No. 3 shall also be deemed discharged from the case.

(6) It appears that case file of the trial Court as well as the appellate Court is called for disposal of the present petition and, therefore, the record of the Courts below be immediately returned to the respective Courts along with the copy of this order so that the trial Court may proceed with the case against the remaining accused persons.
(N.K. GUPTA) JUDGE (05/05/2016) Abhi Suresh Chand Chaurasiya vs State Of M.P. on 5 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10501653/
